Programmable device controllers are increasingly becoming an important part of advanced user workflows, including for agentic programming. Logitech is now officially launching a compact solution onto the market that can be placed anywhere on your desk.

Logitech announced today the MX Keypad, an accessory priced at US$99.99, featuring 9 customisable full-colour LCD keys for quickly launching commands, executing macros and opening AI tools.

The MX Keypad is half the price of the Logitech MX Creative Console.

If this hardware looks familiar, there's a reason. Logitech's MX Creative Console pairs an LCD keypad with a separate dial controller (dialpad), making it easy to adjust settings and perform operations within creative applications.

The MX Keypad retains only the keypad experience, without the extra controller, at half the price of the Creative Console's US$199.99 price tag.

The marketing focus for this new product is developers and AI workflows, but the customisation features actually extend beyond coding.

The entire user experience can be customised through the Logi Options+ application.

Through the free Logi Options+ application, users can assign hotkeys, pre-stored prompts, scripts and macros to each key. The device has two page-switch buttons, supporting up to 15 pages of settings, and the application-aware feature automatically switches profiles when you switch between different applications.

That means the same set of physical keys can serve different functions in VS Code, Slack, Chrome or other applications. The Logi Marketplace offers various plugins, profiles and icon packs, while the built-in icon editor allows users to customise the appearance of each key.

You can use AI to build yourself an AI keyboard.

My initial hands-on test involved connecting the MX Keypad to the MacBook Air on my desk, then having Codex use its computer control capabilities to create custom keys in Logi Options+ based on my ChatGPT usage habits on Mac.

Having an AI coding agent set up physical keys for operating AI is rather poetic, and it clearly states this product's selling point: putting the prompts and actions you frequently use on dedicated, clearly labelled keys.

The MX Keypad is the result of a collaboration between Logitech and GitHub. The product features built-in GitHub Copilot integration for VS Code, and both new and existing users can redeem a 3-month free Copilot Pro+ subscription through Logi Options+.

The MX Keypad supports third-party community plugins.

Logitech also mentioned that plugins developed by the community for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex provide agent status tracking and terminal control features. Developers who want to go further can use the Logi Actions SDK, which supports C# and Node.js, to build custom plugins.

The MX Keypad connects via USB-C and requires macOS 13 or above, or Windows 10 or above. The device measures approximately 3.6 x 3.1 inches and weighs only 96 grams, so it won't take up much space next to your laptop or keyboard.

The MX Keypad goes on sale today (September 8), available in Graphite and Pale Grey, priced at US$99.99.
